controls.label: Infrared color
controls.qualification: False color from its measured flux in three infrared bands (Kraus et al. (2014a), as compiled in Best, Liu, Magnier & Dupuy (2024), The UltracoolSheet v2.1 (Zenodo); zero points from the SVO Filter Profile Service). The disc itself is unresolved; darkening toward the edge from a model atmosphere.
controls.notes: ROXs 42B b's brightness in three infrared bands as one color: red MKO K 2.184 µm, green MKO H 1.614 µm, blue MKO J 1.2417 µm (Kraus et al. (2014a), as compiled in Best, Liu, Magnier & Dupuy (2024), The UltracoolSheet v2.1 (Zenodo); zero points from the SVO Filter Profile Service), on a range shared with this planet alone, from zero to its brightest band (mko k), so the color shows its band ratios; brightness is not compared across planets at different distances. Not a natural color; nobody has resolved its disc. The darkening toward the edge is the quadratic law Claret, Hauschildt & Witte (2012), A&A 546, A14 compute from PHOENIX model atmospheres for the H band at 1,935 K and log g 3.6 (u1 0.666, u2 0.109): a model, not a measurement of this planet.
